system_description.narrative_title: Standoff over reopening the Strait of Hormuz
system_description.narrative_summary: Iran is leveraging control of the Strait of Hormuz to extract political, military, and economic concessions from the United States while pursuing a parallel, Oman-mediated deal and signaling readiness to escalate through targeted attacks. This is an open system of interacting state and non-state actors, security incidents, diplomatic negotiations, energy/shipping flows, and domestic political pressures that generate reinforcing and balancing feedbacks — small incidents can rapidly shift bargaining leverage and regional stability. Key sensitivities include US response options (economic pressure, demands for reparations, military posture), Gulf states' security alignments, and Iran's internal decision-making.
system_description.scope: Negotiations and coercive control over passage through the Strait of Hormuz: Iranian demands and conditions, Oman-mediated talks, US policy and rhetoric, Gulf states' security responses, shipping/energy flow disruptions, and IRGC operations.
system_description.super_system: Global energy markets and international security (trade chokepoints, great-power competition and maritime stability).
adjacent_subsystems: Gulf state security cooperation and military pacts (GCC, Saudi/UAE defense arrangements)
Global oil and maritime shipping markets (supply chains, insurance, tanker routes)
US domestic politics and electoral/calculative pressures on foreign policy
Iranian internal politics and security apparatus (leadership changes, IRGC)

variables.name: Chokepoint control level
variables.description: The degree to which passage through the maritime chokepoint is under coercive or effective control by actors in the area.

variables.name: Coercive leverage
variables.description: The aggregate bargaining power available to actors that arises from threats to disrupt transit, commerce, or security in the corridor.

variables.name: Escalation readiness
variables.description: The preparedness and willingness of actors to escalate kinetic or paramilitary actions in the maritime domain.

variables.name: Security incident rate
variables.description: The frequency of hostile or destabilizing security incidents (attacks, seizures, strikes) affecting vessels or infrastructure per unit time.

variables.name: Maritime throughput rate
variables.description: The volume and rate of commercial and energy-related shipping transiting the chokepoint per unit time.

variables.name: Energy market sensitivity
variables.description: The responsiveness of global energy markets to disruptions or perceived risks to flows through the chokepoint.

variables.name: Negotiation intensity
variables.description: The tempo and resource commitment of diplomatic negotiations focused on access, transit conditions, or conflict de-escalation.

variables.name: Mediation effectiveness
variables.description: The capacity of third-party diplomatic channels and mediation processes to resolve disputes and produce durable agreements.

variables.name: Military presence level
variables.description: The overall density and posture of naval and military assets operating in and around the chokepoint region.

variables.name: Regional alignment
variables.description: The degree of security cooperation, coordination, or collective posture among neighboring actors regarding chokepoint security.

variables.name: Economic pressure
variables.description: The magnitude of economic coercion applied to actors through trade restrictions, asset measures, or financial measures.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure
variables.description: The intensity of internal political constraints and incentives on leadership decisions related to confrontation or concession.

variables.name: Shipping risk perception
variables.description: The perceived risk level among commercial maritime stakeholders about transiting the chokepoint.

variables.name: Insurance premium level
variables.description: The prevailing cost and volatility of maritime insurance premiums for vessels operating in or near the chokepoint.

variables.name: Information opacity
variables.description: The degree of uncertainty about actors' intentions, capabilities, and internal decision-making communicated externally.

variables.name: Coercer economic resilience
variables.description: The capacity of the coercing actor(s) to withstand economic isolation or pressure while sustaining coercive posture.

catalysts.title: Oman–Iran Hormuz agreement closes
catalysts.description: A formal Oman–Iran agreement to reopen/route shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is finalized and announced, enabling resumed transit under new terms.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Negotiators Close In on Deal With Iran to Open Hormuz"; "US expects deal soon on Strait of Hormuz".

catalysts.title: Iran ties reopening to US concessions
catalysts.description: Iran conditions reopening on explicit U.S. concessions (reparations, withdrawals, behaviour changes), raising bargaining demands and prolonging standoff.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Iran sets conditions for opening Strait of Hormuz"; "Iran ties Hormuz reopening to US concessions."

catalysts.title: U.S. shifts to intensified economic pressure
catalysts.description: U.S. public demands for reparations and stated focus on economic pain drive an escalation in sanctions/financial pressure aimed at Iran.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Trump Shifts to Economic Pressure"; "Trump says Iran must pay compensation."

catalysts.title: Iranian hard-line security consolidation
catalysts.description: Leadership and security-service changes consolidate a harder stance, reducing willingness to compromise and raising operational readiness.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Iran replaces top security official"; "Mysterious Ruler Signals a Hard Line."

catalysts.title: Gulf states formalize defense coordination
catalysts.description: Sunni Gulf states deepen defense cooperation or form a pact to deter threats to shipping and counter Iranian coercion.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Sunni powers unite in defense pact"; "Gulf States Accept a New Normal in Hormuz: Iran Is in Control."

catalysts.title: Sustained decline in shipping through Hormuz
catalysts.description: Commercial throughput continues to fall and insurance premiums rise as deal prospects fade and risk perceptions harden.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Gulf shipping through Strait of Hormuz reportedly falls as Iran deal hopes fade."

catalysts.title: Ongoing Houthi/region maritime attacks
catalysts.description: Continued strikes/claims by Houthis and attacks on vessels or facilities sustain a high incident tempo in the corridor.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Houthis claim attack on Saudi refinery"; "UAE says Iran attacked ADNOC vessel."

catalysts.title: Negotiations stall over alleged interim-deal breaches
catalysts.description: Talks between the US and Iran pause or fail to resume because Iran says interim deal has been breached and conditions remain unmet.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Talks with US won't happen while interim deal is breached"; "Iran says deal is close but not enough to open the waterway."
